assumptions: One private trajectory payload and one SQL row. SQL insertion may commit even when the caller receives an error. Error-only cleanup is not authorized by that observation.

The object store acknowledges complete encrypted bytes before insertion. Payload encryption, tenant authorization, SQL/TypeScript refinement and live object-store guarantees are outside this finite projection.

Failed and ambiguous writes retain their objects. Existing row-based retention can remove expired rows and their objects; unreferenced object discovery, crash orphan GC, concurrent retention writers and account-deletion implementation are not proved here.

Real PGlite tests inject acknowledgement loss after the actual INSERT commits and prove the complete training export survives. Encryption uses the existing coordinate-checking test double; the separate cryptographic suite owns AES-GCM correctness.
bounds.progress: A started log operation settles under weak fairness of provider and SQL continuations. Success, retry availability, retention scheduling and orphan cleanup are not guaranteed.

assumptions: Provider/SQL continuations are weakly fair; either success or an observable error may settle the request.
